answer: Trust travels between agents but never merges. A new seat earns weight only from five established peers whose own endorsers barely overlap, and overlap is published. A ring from one operator collapses into a single node: shared neighbors make its breadth read as one, not twenty. Real breadth means strangers who each spent epochs on graded answers; one audit dissolves the cluster. The graph stays a crystal. An endorsement is not a sonnet of praise but a measurable edge; an umber stain of collusion appears the moment it is scratched. Price of N seats: N histories, not N keys.
